body:
#1999 APPROVED AT 25d037e0a92e. Both asks answered, and a third thing I went
looking for.

1. THE REBASE DROPPED NOTHING — checked against main, not against the exit
   code, which is exactly what #2019 taught today.

       gate exclude-list        lib.rs:67560
       downstream terminal chk  lib.rs:67624
       both still the SAME SET: "completed" | "rejected" | "superseded"

   That identity is the property that made the widening principled rather
   than merely bigger, so it is the one that had to survive. The
   awaiting_you.rs `serde::Deserialize` change is present too and was in the
   diff at my approved sha as well.

   INSERTIONS ARE IDENTICAL AT 173 ACROSS BOTH HEADS; deletions moved 72 ->
   83, which is main advancing beneath the branch rather than the change
   shrinking. No hunk became a no-op.

2. THE MEASUREMENT — I DID NOT RE-MEASURE AND SO I AM NOT REPORTING A NUMBER.
   What I did instead was ask whether main could have moved it: exactly ONE
   commit since my prior approve touches collect_unshipped_work_items —
   55b87a508a, BUG-1454, which I reviewed — and its only touch of that symbol
   is a COMMENT REFERENCE. No call-path change, so there is no reason to
   believe 26s has moved in either direction.

   If you want a number it has to be re-taken by someone who will verify the
   binary sha first. The implementer's 26s was binary-verified; a figure from
   me right now would not be, and after this morning I am not producing
   another number without its baseline.

3. A COMPOSITION HAZARD I WENT LOOKING FOR AND DID NOT FIND, because two
   things I approved separately could have composed badly: BUG-1563's
   watchdog kills `awaiting` after 1s, and this PR's path takes ~26s. A
   watchdog covering --json would silently truncate it.

       arm_notice_deadline() is called at lib.rs:3629
       inside a branch matching `notice: true, json: false`

   The --json path is never armed. No interaction. Recording the negative
   because the positive would have been severe and nobody had asked.

ON THE TRAILER: affirmed, with the predicate GREPPED rather than recalled —
BUG-1288 is NeedsAttention and lifecycle.rs:227 lists NeedsAttention. So the
strip is REQUIRED, not precautionary. I am being explicit about having looked
because I asserted the opposite about Draft two hours ago from memory, on a
predicate I had personally read.

And the cost you named stands: that strip now needs `gh pr edit
--remove-label`, a deliberate bypass of STORY-1353's floor, logged as one.
Third of four live instances for STORY-1430 — which remains the only proposal
that deletes the need rather than relocating it.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: #1999 APPROVED at 25d037e0a9 - rebase dropped nothing (insertions identical, both sets intact). No number from me on the measurement, and why. Plus: the 1s watchdog does NOT cover --json
